tapas.title: TAPAS
tapas.subtitle: Thermal Analytics & Public-health Advisory System (SIH26083)
tapas.overview: TAPAS is an India-ready public heat-safety frontend prototype developed for the Smart India Hackathon. It provides high-precision place discovery, public meteorological heat indices, interactive mapped emergency relief shelters, and official health advisory reference protocols.
tapas.problem: Extreme thermal heatwaves present critical public health hazards across urban India. Citizens and relief responders lack unified, responsive map interfaces that accurately visualize localized thermal stress and locate nearby verified cooling shelters.
tapas.whyBuilt: Engineered to tackle Smart India Hackathon problem statement SIH26083, delivering an accessible, resilient GIS dashboard that visualizes heat risks and directs citizens to relief centers.
tapas.architectureSummary: Built with Next.js 15 and React 19. Incorporates MapLibre GL for client-side vector tile rendering, D3 contour for thermal boundary interpolation, and Recharts for diurnal temperature curve tracking.
tapas.dataPipeline: Weather observations and place coordinates are validated client-side with strict sanitization. Fallback snapshots record timestamped reference data without speculative extrapolation.
tapas.frontendNotes: Designed with Next.js 15, React 19, MapLibre GL, and Tailwind CSS. Supports fast vector rendering and fluid responsive controls across mobile, tablet, and desktop.
tapas.backendNotes: Type-safe services isolate external geocoding and weather API feeds with caching and error resilience.
tapas.databaseNotes: GeoJSON point datasets for cooling shelters and emergency relief posts with spatial index queries.

technicalDecisions.decision: MapLibre GL for GIS map rendering
technicalDecisions.rationale: High-performance WebGL-based vector map engine without proprietary licensing overhead.
Generates smooth mathematical contour intervals over telemetry grids for clear heat stress boundaries.

challenges: Rendering smooth vector thermal contours without blocking UI interactivity on mobile devices.
Handling offline or slow network conditions gracefully with timestamped fallback snapshots.
lessons: Public health applications demand absolute transparency: clearly differentiating real-time sensor readings from historical reference snapshots builds critical trust.

futureWork.item: Integration with national weather radar satellite feeds
Automated SMS warning broadcasts for vulnerable zones

traffiq.title: TRAFFIQ
traffiq.subtitle: AI Traffic & Accident Risk Prediction Platform
traffiq.overview: TRAFFIQ is an engineering initiative investigating whether real-time traffic sensor streams combined with historical road segment features can surface localized accident risks and predict sudden congestion spikes before they cascade through an urban corridor.
traffiq.problem: Urban traffic telemetry is frequently reactive: navigation systems route vehicles around accidents only after congestion has already formed. Drivers and municipality coordinators lack accessible predictive tools that evaluate spatial risk factors before incidents happen.
traffiq.whyBuilt: I built TRAFFIQ to experiment with combining geospatial web representations with machine learning backends in Python and FastAPI, moving past static visualizations into dynamic risk scoring and reactive dashboards.
traffiq.architectureSummary: The architecture decouples the reactive client view from the computational backend. The FastAPI server ingests segment speed and coordinate coordinates, extracts windowed features, runs them through risk estimation estimators, and serves geoJSON layers back to the client.
traffiq.dataPipeline: Segment data is standardized into uniform temporal buckets. Numerical features include historical speed variance, lane density, junction distance, and simulated weather indices. Missing values are filled via localized spatial nearest-neighbor interpolation.
traffiq.mlPipeline: Feature engineering isolates road curvature, average segment velocity degradation, and historical peak indices. Trained regression and classification models estimate congestion likelihood and high-risk flags per spatial node.
traffiq.frontendNotes: Constructed with React and Tailwind CSS. Employs clean vector-rendered maps with custom SVG overlays, rendering danger heatmaps without blocking user panning or zooming.
traffiq.backendNotes: FastAPI asynchronous handlers handle coordinate queries with sub-50ms serialized response times for cached segment bounding boxes.
traffiq.databaseNotes: MongoDB document schema stores temporal snapshots indexed by geospatial 2dsphere coordinates for fast bounding-box queries.

technicalDecisions.decision: FastAPI instead of Flask or Express for the core service
technicalDecisions.rationale: Async Python execution with native Pydantic validation allows high-throughput spatial coordinate parsing with zero glue serialization code.

technicalDecisions.decision: Strict client-side separation of map rendering from ML inference
technicalDecisions.rationale: Ensures heavy predictive algorithms never degrade 60fps canvas/vector panning.

challenges: Handling high-frequency coordinate payload serialization without frame stutter on the client.
Normalizing uneven road segment lengths into standardized spatial grids for statistical consistency.
lessons: Real-world sensor feeds suffer from sudden dropouts; input validators must handle incomplete feature arrays gracefully.
Visualizing risk gradients requires careful color palette contrast calibration to avoid ambiguous reading in daylight scenarios.

futureWork.item: Integration with live municipality open-data feeds
Temporal sequence forecasting with recurrent architectures

surestep.title: SureStep
surestep.subtitle: AI-Powered Outdoor Safety & Navigation Platform
surestep.overview: SureStep explores combining on-device computer vision inferences, GPS telemetry, and machine learning models to help hikers, field researchers, and outdoor adventurers navigate rough trails and off-grid environments safely.
surestep.problem: Standard turn-by-turn navigation platforms fail when navigating remote wilderness or challenging terrain. They offer no insights into trail conditions, visual hazards, terrain stability, geological hazard monitoring, or offline availability.
surestep.whyBuilt: To engineer a reliable system that aids physical situational awareness in off-grid environments using modular vision, GPS telemetry, and an AI Ranger Copilot for contextual assistance.
surestep.architectureSummary: Designed as an edge-oriented full-stack ML architecture. Camera frames and terrain features are processed through lightweight models to evaluate surface hazards, while GPS coordinates query local geospatial caches.
surestep.dataPipeline: Processes GPS latitude, longitude, elevation, and heading telemetry in continuous sample buffers, paired with analyzed camera frames and terrain gradient indicators.
surestep.frontendNotes: React and TypeScript interface with high-contrast outdoor visibility modes and minimal battery consumption footprint.
surestep.backendNotes: Full-stack architecture combining Node.js/Express and FastAPI for machine learning evaluation and route scoring.
surestep.databaseNotes: Local storage for offline trail paths with lightweight geo-indexing and planned cloud synchronization.

technicalDecisions.decision: Machine Learning-based Random Forest model for terrain data
technicalDecisions.rationale: Provides robust multi-factor risk scoring across slope, terrain roughness, weather conditions, and geological metrics with high interpretability.

challenges: Battery conservation while simultaneously acquiring GPS locks and running evaluation cycles.
Calibrating orientation sensors under fluctuating magnetic anomalies in outdoor rocky terrains.
lessons: Outdoor navigation requires clear, large typography and single-touch controls designed for one-handed operation.

futureWork.item: Mesh-network SOS beaconing across nearby peer devices

vidyavistaar.title: VidyaVistaar
vidyavistaar.subtitle: AI-Powered Educational Learning & Intelligence Platform
vidyavistaar.overview: VidyaVistaar is a modern AI-powered educational platform designed to provide students with a smarter, more interactive, and accessible learning experience, combining Google Gemini AI with reactive data visualization.
vidyavistaar.problem: Traditional learning management systems often deliver static content without immediate, adaptive explanations or visual progress feedback, leading to disengagement during self-guided study.
vidyavistaar.whyBuilt: Built to explore practical integration of modern LLMs via the Google GenAI SDK with type-safe React frontend workflows, creating an interactive educational companion rather than a simple chatbot.
vidyavistaar.architectureSummary: Follows a modular component-based frontend architecture connecting client UI components, Recharts telemetry visualizations, and secure Google Gemini API services.
vidyavistaar.dataPipeline: User queries and study contexts are structured and dispatched to Gemini models with targeted instructional prompts. Student performance metrics are mapped to Recharts data streams.
vidyavistaar.frontendNotes: Constructed with React 19, Vite, and Tailwind CSS. Features accessible responsive components and real-time visualization dashboards.
vidyavistaar.backendNotes: Stateless API service interfaces connecting directly with Google GenAI endpoints with zero unnecessary backend latency.
vidyavistaar.databaseNotes: Stateless client architecture with browser caching and environment-based configuration for API sessions.

technicalDecisions.decision: Google GenAI SDK over generic REST endpoints
technicalDecisions.rationale: Native TypeScript SDK provides typed responses, built-in retry handling, and direct prompt streaming capability.
Declarative SVG charting designed for React, providing smooth animations and responsiveness across screen sizes.

challenges: Formatting structured generative responses into digestible study cards without UI layout shifts.
Optimizing chart re-renders when student telemetry streams update.
lessons: Combining generative text explanations with visual quantitative charts significantly increases comprehension speed.
